name: Greeley
title: Artificial Turf in Greeley, CO — Front-Yard Rule | NoCo Turf Co.
description: Greeley bars turf from house front yards and from street view in new development; a front-yard permit was still a draft on September 24, 2026.
h1: Greeley still keeps turf out of front yards while a permit rule waits
lede: Greeley's turf rules are mid-rewrite. As of September 24, 2026, the rule on the books still stands, and it is about what the street can see.

answer.question: Can I put artificial turf in my front yard in Greeley?
answer.answer: Not yet. NoCo Turf Co. installs artificial turf in Greeley, Colorado, where city staff say turf is prohibited in the front yards of houses. A draft change would allow it by permit, but no ordinance had been adopted as of September 24, 2026. Backyards the street can't see are where turf fits today.

blocks.h2: Greeley keeps artificial turf out of house front yards, and out of street view in new development.
paras: Greeley Municipal Code Section 24-802, adopted as Ordinance No. 36 in 2021, says that in new development artificial turf is only acceptable as ground cover for areas not visible from public rights-of-way and streets, and may be subject to engineering specifications tied to grading or drainage plans. City staff put it plainly for the Planning Commission on July 14, 2026: artificial turf is prohibited in the front yards of houses.
That makes a fenced backyard the place for turf in Greeley today. A corner lot's side yard, which the street can see, is a question for the city before you design it.

blocks.h2: A front-yard permit path is drafted, not adopted.
paras: Council Initiative 11-2023 would let houses put artificial turf in the front yard with a permit, keep trees and live plantings required, and require an installer who is licensed or certified. Staff presented the landscape standards to Council at a work session in July 2026.

As of September 24, 2026 the initiative's status still read 'Come back to Council with a draft ordinance,' and no ordinance had been adopted. Until one is, the current rules stand, so check the city's current code before you sign for any front-yard design.

blocks.h2: Greeley bills by a water budget, and the price climbs once you pass it.
paras: Single-family homes inside the city pay $6.18 per 1,000 gallons within their budget in 2026, $7.16 at 101–130%, $9.76 at 131–150% and $13.01 above 151%, plus a $21.00 fixed monthly charge.

Greeley declared 2026 an adequate water year on April 15, so normal watering guidelines hold through October 31, backed by Northern Water's 0.8 acre-foot quota per Colorado-Big Thompson unit. Homes in the northern part of the city can be on North Weld County Water District instead, which asked for voluntary limits of three days a week in 2026.
The city's 2026 residential rebates cover high-efficiency toilets and irrigation equipment only. There is no lawn-replacement or turf rebate.

blocks.h2: Greeley's sandy topsoil can sit just inches above hard clay.
paras: Greeley's water department says soils in the area tend to be shallow, with a layer of hard clay sometimes just inches below the surface. Soil surveys around central Greeley map mostly low shrink-swell sandy soils, Olney fine sandy loam and Otero sandy loam.
For a turf base, find out which one you have before digging: sand drains through an aggregate base, while a clay layer a few inches down holds water under it.

blocks.h2: 48 of Greeley's 53 metro districts were formed in 2018 or later.
paras: By the state's district map, 53 metro districts have a representative point inside Greeley, and 48 of them formed in 2018 or later, led by the Delantero, Cache and Union Colony West families.

The established half of the city is just as large: Weber West, Rolling Hills, Country Club West and Farr's are among the biggest subdivisions by residential parcels, and the median house lot is about 7,511 square feet.

blocks.h2: Greeley averages 58.3 days a year at 90°F or hotter.
paras: The Greeley UNC station averages 58.3 days at or above 90°F and 6.5 days at or above 100°F, with 14.65 inches of precipitation and 34.9 inches of snow (1991–2020 normals). NOAA logged 37 hail reports referenced to Greeley from 2011 through 2025, the largest 2 inches on July 29, 2016.

sections.name: LaSalle
paras: LaSalle, just south of Greeley, sets its own watering rules under Resolution H-2026 through December 31, 2026: no watering on Fridays, none from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., and new sod or seed only by permit. The Dove Hill subdivision runs a separate non-potable system, scheduled to shut off September 30, 2026.

LaSalle's municipal code, codified through Ord. 5-2026, has no artificial-turf provision; its one cap on non-living ground cover, 20%, applies to parking-lot setbacks. Treated water comes from Central Weld County Water District, and about 72.8% of LaSalle's homes were built before 1980.

sections.name: Platteville
paras: Platteville writes installation quality into its nuisance code. Under Section 7-1-30(s), permitting or maintaining artificial turf that was not installed in a professional manner to the manufacturer's specifications is a public nuisance; the examples are seams that aren't tight, edges that aren't fastened, turf not laid over an aggregate base, and waves.

Drinking water comes from Central Weld County Water District, and the town's page says watering is not allowed between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m.; even addresses water Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday, odd addresses Saturday, Monday and Wednesday.
The town sits on the east bank of the South Platte beside Fort Vasquez, and its Harvest Daze festival has run each August since 1910.

faq.q: When will Greeley allow front-yard turf?
faq.a: It depends on Council. As of September 24, 2026, Council Initiative 11-2023 was still at 'come back to Council with a draft ordinance,' and nothing had been adopted. Until an ordinance passes, turf in the front yard of a house is not allowed.

faq.q: If Greeley's change passes, who could install front-yard turf?
faq.a: The draft calls for a permit, continued trees and live plantings, and an installer who is licensed or certified. The final ordinance language has not been written.

faq.q: Does Greeley offer a rebate for artificial turf?
faq.a: No. Greeley's 2026 residential rebates cover high-efficiency toilets and irrigation systems only.

faq.q: What does Platteville require of a turf install?
faq.a: That it be done professionally and to the manufacturer's specifications. Under Section 7-1-30(s), loose seams, unfastened edges, no aggregate base or waves can make turf a public nuisance.
